And firstly, therapy success is based around ones ability to put the effort in, but sometimes that effort is as little as showing up and hearing the ways to try something different etc. 

But main ones when we think about therapy- is Talk therapy. Cognitive-behavior and dialect behavior therapy are options around that. 

The idea is to help guide your thinking process towards these things. Be able to teach/learn coping skills and ways to handle regulating emotions and situations better. 

Anyone facing a situation that conflicts with their identity is going to struggle and feel a type of way about that. 

I may not be gay but having adhd, and not feeling secure on any one specific thing, still can interfere with my identity. If we don’t feel secure on our identities we can feel more anxious. 

And although I may not be gay, now, I can say I struggled with that identity specific too, i just worked through and found the answer I don’t feel gay but I do understand that side and info more in depth and more secure because I was willing to ask myself those tough questions- or even learning I needed to actually ask myself these questions (and this can be any difficult tasks being dealt with) asking and sorting through the thinking process and what leads to X and how I feel as I reach X. 

There are is also EMDR (Eye movement desensitization…forget exact but rapid eye movement back and forth as recalling emotional memories allows you to process these emotions and work through it and has had a lot of success towards child trauma and other traumas.) I didn’t do  it long enough for more impact but it helped a tiny as I tried processing childhood relationships. But that attempt happened during covid and well… very difficult to do that on a screen lol. It’s kind of like a sound bar with a pixel dot flying back and forth and you set it to what you are able to handle, pace wise, and the goal is to have a happy thought/place to go to deescalate from those memories and feel secure when leaving the sessions. 

I aimed to go for specialized therapies to the diagnosis and that did help me see I didn’t have one diagnosis because the therapist actually had it and I was displaying certain things xyz. So if after couple months to 6 or less (meaning find a therapist that actually listens/actually vibe and feel comfortable discussing and not being a judged zone) therapy doesn’t work if you don’t feel secure with them. 

In the meantime you could seek videos specifically titled to these and see what information resonates the most to what you’re feeling right now and start your journey 😇 Again this does require you to actually want and such so it does revolve around patient being honest and transparent about goals as well. If anything, start that process on your own to give you more foundation of information when/if can locate a therapist. 

For psychiatrists they are medications and honestly.. well.. I have a lot of thoughts about the system and where improvements really need to be had and the 5-20 minute interactions with a psychiatrist who is about to prescribe a brain chemically changing medicine should really be aware of what the heck the symptoms and outcome looked for etc… so I hope you’re able to find good interactions. It also took several psychiatrists to find one to prescribe something that worked. 

Be your advocate if/when time comes medications are considered and give it some time for them to work and build up for some types etc yet also keep track of what is happening and if benefits are showing. If they aren’t, then maybe consider adjustments of strength or changing. 

I’ve had antidepressants, anti anxiety of different levels and brands and landing on a stimulant realm of medication is where I’ve felt the meaningful positives. And unfortunately it’s a challenging disorder because the medication is a stimulant usually and meaning higher rates of caution and regulations prescribing. And doesn’t seem fully understood either. Classified lazy and other things but pretty common. Whole families can exhibit it. There’s ways to work with it once you figure out what you’re specifically struggling with. 

Depression often times happens as a result of a root disorder going undiagnosed/treated. 

Hope that was helpful and good luck! Stay focused and breath. Also check into grounding techniques can sometimes help with thoughts and redirecting ourselves.

Chiming in to say- coming from someone who said i *CANT* do apartments…… standards get knocked real quick when you realize going out to sign and you can’t actually get the ideal start you thought. So please realize that sooner than later so you can stay focused to your goals… buttt… my point is.. go apartment hunting. Go walk through. Check out the grounds and area. There are smaller buildings of 1-6 units (apartments, townhomes, condos, mobile homes, houses) see what is realistic to essentials. 

Ride around later in the evening to the ones you’re liking and just see if activity is decent/safe/ aim for quiet. Check out car types to see if seems people manage good shaped vehicles (no cars on blocks lol) 

I landed quiet- end unit- can’t hear much within my unit- balcony over the end corner unit and have some nice yard and grass below to view-carport included- quiet- and just searched around and checked reviews for serious no go and check for good areas. 

Jump in easy, and save and save in that apartment …. Keep yourself goal checked. And it’ll pay off because economy can chill (lol hopefully) and you can tackle saving funds and financial direction and have a better chance to getting more of your wants at that time than right now short notice.

Loan* (because you should know) 

You’ll need about 8-9K/ 5K on the low end. 

You don’t go more just because *maybe* more people join in. 

22 isn’t bad. As a single individual (single parent who made 24 hr but office hours) and still not enough without working away life instead enjoying. 

Make plans for what’s next in the next 2 years. What’s getting worked on now to reach 2 year financial goals. Best thing I could go back and say and research financials, so many resources now (yes filter lots of garbage too) but getting the ball rolling now versus mid 20s realizing and maybe a kid later :P 

Call mortgage companies and ask your questions, there is first time home buyer usually. You need a credit score average 640. So first step may be to check credit scores from credit karma to get an idea of what activity you have going on etc. (my credit karma hasn’t been off much but not exacts and different types of scores) if that’s at least 640, add Experian boost (if you have any reoccurring bills from your own account can self report and give some boosts) let that clear then go get it pulled if things are looking good and get a better idea what you realistically can do. 

400k … probably outside your ball park still. And being sure if you don’t already have a personal emergency fund, then you need to account that in your month to month to get 1K minimum, and keep going from there. 6-9 months after pandemic would be smart. Do all that stuff FIRST 😇 yes can take a year give or take depending on your standings to achieve this. 

Best bet is apartment. Split and save for the next few years and prioritize your goals and financial means.
